title: Stakeholder Analysis
intro: Value Sensitive Design asks you to account for everyone a technology affects — not only the people who use it. In this lesson you will build a stakeholder map with tokens: place stakeholders on rings around what you are designing, connect them, note what each could gain or lose, and trace those harms and benefits to the values at stake. The board carries over from step to step, so you can go back and revise at any point. No project of your own? Use a reading app that tracks each student’s progress and shares it with teachers and parents.

steps.title: Choose a starting point
steps.task: Start from a technology, a value, or a context of use. Select the centre of the board and name what you are designing.
objectives: Names a specific technology, value, or context of use
Says which of the three it is

guide.label: The centre of the board
guide.where: Select it, then name it in the panel on the right.

steps.title: Direct stakeholders
steps.task: Add the people who will interact with the technology or its outputs. Drag each token onto the rings: the closer to the centre, the more central they are to the design.
objectives: Identifies the groups who interact with the technology directly
Names stakeholders as roles (e.g. “teachers”), not individuals
Places core stakeholders nearer the centre than peripheral ones

guide.label: Direct token
guide.where: In the palette left of the board. Drag it onto the rings, then type its name.

steps.title: Indirect stakeholders
steps.task: Add the people affected by the technology who never use it. Look for those who are easy to miss: move anyone currently left out of the design into the outer “excluded” area, and flag stakeholders who are hidden or easily overlooked.
objectives: Identifies at least two indirect stakeholder groups
Surfaces hidden, overlooked, or excluded groups
Distinguishes direct from indirect stakeholders correctly

guide.label: Indirect token
guide.where: In the palette left of the board.

guide.label: Excluded area
guide.where: The outer dashed ring. Drag left-out stakeholders there.

guide.label: Hidden or overlooked
guide.where: Right panel, after you select a stakeholder.

steps.title: Relationships between stakeholders
steps.task: Connect stakeholders who affect one another: drag from a token’s dot to another token. Then label how one affects the other (e.g. “reports to”, “cares for”, “pays for”), or, if it goes both ways, mark it mutual and say how they relate (e.g. “share a home”).
objectives: Connects stakeholders whose interests are linked
Labels each relationship with how one affects the other, or how they relate
Marks whether each relationship goes one way or both ways

guide.label: Connections
guide.where: Drag from a token’s dot to another token, or use “Connect to…” in the right panel. Select a connection to set its direction.

steps.title: Harms and benefits
steps.task: Select each stakeholder and note what they could gain or lose from the technology.
objectives: Lists at least one harm or benefit for each stakeholder
Includes harms for indirect stakeholders, not only for users

guide.label: + Harm / + Benefit
guide.where: Right panel, after you select a stakeholder.

steps.title: Map to values
steps.task: For each harm and benefit, name the human values it touches (e.g. privacy, autonomy, trust, fairness).
objectives: Links each harm and benefit to one or more values
Chooses values with ethical import, not only usability features

guide.label: + value
guide.where: Under each harm and benefit in the right panel. Type a value and press Enter.

steps.title: Define the key values
steps.task: For the values that matter most, write what each one means in this context. Different stakeholders may understand the same value differently.
objectives: Defines key values in terms of this technology and its stakeholders
Notes where stakeholders would understand a value differently

guide.label: Value definitions
guide.where: In the Values list at the bottom of the right panel.

steps.title: Value tensions
steps.task: Draw a tension between two stakeholders whose values pull against each other, and name the value at stake for each (e.g. a student’s privacy vs a parent’s wish to stay informed).
objectives: Identifies at least one tension between stakeholders’ values
Names the specific value in conflict on each side

guide.label: Tensions
guide.where: “Tension with…” in the right panel, or switch dragging to “Tension” left of the board.

steps.title: Take it into the organization
steps.task: For the key values and tensions, note who should own them and what they will do next.
objectives: Assigns an owner to each key value or tension
Proposes a concrete next action for each

guide.label: Owner and next action
guide.where: Under each value, and in each tension.
